title: Role of AI in the analysis of total knee arthroplasty.
summary: The model showed modest association with one-year KOOS and infection discrimination, with systematic score and risk calibration errors. Retrospective 98-patient cohort, internal analysis only; no external validation or prospective clinical-impact testing. No same-result active/archive match.
ai_technology: ChatGPT-based AI predicts one-year KOOS and infection outcomes from retrospective total-knee-arthroplasty records.
organization: Department of Orthopedics, Kalinga Institute of Medical Sciences, KIIT, Bhubaneswar, Odisha, India

evidence.ai_role: ChatGPT-based AI predicts one-year KOOS and infection outcomes from retrospective total-knee-arthroplasty records.
evidence.tested: The model showed modest association with one-year KOOS and infection discrimination, with systematic score and risk calibration errors.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective 98-patient cohort, internal analysis only; no external validation or prospective clinical-impact testing. No same-result active/archive match.

source_review.scope: The retrospective study analyzes 98 total-knee-arthroplasty patients and reports ChatGPT-based prediction of one-year KOOS and infection outcomes (KOOS correlation about 0.45; infection ROC-AUC about 0.70), with systematic KOOS underprediction and infection overestimation. This is a specific clinical prediction result, not evidence of clinical utility; it lacks external validation. Adjacent TKA catalog entries address different outcomes/models.
